Decision Tool

Maintenance Budget Planner

A planning-grade annual budget range for proactive roof maintenance — inspections, housekeeping, and minor repairs — based on system, age, and size. Built to start a budget conversation, not end one.

Source verification in progress Updated July 15, 2026 Editorial standards · Report an error
Source verification in progressSources for this page are still being verified. Details may change.

Your roof

Enter a size between 1,000 and 2,000,000 sq ft.
Reactive roofs usually need a first-year catch-up allowance.

Planning-grade annual budget

—

Methodology v0.1 — rates are pre-validation placeholders, flagged pending the CRI cost benchmark dataset. Full methodology below.

What this budget covers — and doesn't Covers the proactive program: scheduled inspections, drain and housekeeping work, and minor repairs. It does not fund capital events (coating cycles, section replacement, storm damage) — those are planned separately, and this tool tells you when to start that conversation.

Methodology

The planner multiplies roof area by a per-square-foot annual maintenance rate range, adjusted for system and age:

  • Base rates (placeholder, pre-validation): single-ply $0.10–$0.25/sf·yr; asphalt multi-ply $0.12–$0.30; metal $0.05–$0.15; coated $0.08–$0.20.
  • Age: 0–5 yrs ×0.7 · 6–15 yrs ×1.0 · 16+ yrs ×1.5.
  • Reactive posture: one-time first-year catch-up allowance of 50–100% of the annual figure, shown separately.
  • Results round to sensible increments; ranges are wide by design at v0.1.

These rates are drawn from commonly published industry planning figures and are explicitly unvalidated placeholders until the CRI cost benchmark dataset (v1.0) replaces them — the same standard as the Life Expectancy Estimator.

Limitations

  • National planning ranges; regional labor rates shift them meaningfully.
  • Excludes capital events, storm response, and warranty-required specialist work.
  • Roofs with chronic defects need a condition assessment before a budget means anything.
